Body: This is not true.  We don't use a special behavior for `0`.  If the value is 0 we WANT it to fallback to the base model.

I don't think this is helpful either.  For variant context limits we care about the _context window limits_, not the model's output token ceiling.

I could be wrong about this...
Same as before.  We WANT this behavior on purpose
This is decent feedback, but minor.

This override is applied after the semantic mapping in `resolveThemeVariantV2()`, so OC-2 still resolves `bg-layer-04` to the pre-tuning colors (`grey-400` here and `grey-700` in dark mode). Please regenerate `oc-2.json` with `packages/ui/script/build-oc2-v2-overrides.ts` after updating `theme.css` so the open-tab indicator receives the tuned values.

Non-blocking follow-up: these four visible labels are not associated with their inputs. `TextInputV2` renders a sibling `<input>` and does not create that association, so clicking a label will not focus the field and assistive technology will not announce the visible label. Could we add matching `for`/`id` attributes (or equivalent accessible labels) in a follow-up?
NO fx
`grey-400` and `gray-700` is correct as per Figma, I only changed the tokens for generated themes to bring their contrast closer to OC-2
Actually, the **other** OC-2 tokens were outdated; the design system must've been updated... I made a quick PR to fix: [#31071](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/31071)

`at` uses `updated || created`, which treats `0` as falsy. Since timestamps are numbers and `0` is a valid epoch value, this can incorrectly fall back to `created` and bucket the record on the wrong day. Use nullish coalescing (or just reuse the `updated` value you already computed) so only `null`/`undefined` trigger fallback.

When no token data exists (`peakTokens === 0`), `value/level/streaks/hasActivity` switch to using `count`, but the returned shape still exposes only token-focused aggregates (`totalTokens`, `peakTokens`) and the UI labels everything as “tokens”. Since `tokens` on records is optional, this can produce a heatmap driven by session counts while the summary/tooltip reads “0 tokens …”. Consider making the metric explicit in the API (e.g., `metric: 'tokens' | 'sessions'`), and return matching totals/peaks for that metric, or remove the `count` fallback and treat missing token data as “no token activity”.

Each heatmap cell is a non-focusable `<div>`, but the tooltip relies on `group-focus-visible` for keyboard access. As-is, keyboard users can’t focus cells to discover per-day values. Make the cell focusable (e.g., `tabIndex=0` with appropriate role) or use a semantic interactive element and provide an accessible name/description (or an `aria-label`) per cell.

Home now loads up to 360 sessions per project directory, concurrently, on a single query. This is a significant increase from 64 and can amplify startup latency/memory/network usage for users with many projects. Consider reducing concurrency (queue/throttle), fetching only what the activity window needs (or a dedicated aggregated endpoint), and/or limiting the data processed for the heatmap to the same cap actually fetched.

`HOME_ACTIVITY_WEEKS` is derived via division and can become non-integer if `HOME_ACTIVITY_DAYS` changes, which would break `repeat(weekCount, ...)` grid rendering and month span calculations. Consider defining `HOME_ACTIVITY_WEEKS` as an integer (e.g., `Math.ceil(HOME_ACTIVITY_DAYS / 7)`) and ensuring day `column` math stays consistent with the chosen rounding.

`backend` is typed as `UpdaterBackend`, but the object literal includes an `on(...)` method (and the accompanying `listeners` map) that is not part of the `UpdaterBackend` type. With TypeScript excess-property checks (and `strict: true`), this will fail typechecking and the `listeners` variable is unused in the test anyway.

`platform.updater?.install()` returns `Promise<void> | undefined`, so chaining `.then/.catch` on it is unsafe (and should fail under `strict` TS). If `platform.updater` is ever undefined, this will throw at runtime when trying to access `.then` on `undefined`.

When `platform.updater` is missing (e.g. non-desktop platforms), `platform.updater?.state()` yields `undefined` and `updaterAction(undefined)` currently falls through to the `default` case, enabling the button with `run: "check"` even though there is no updater to run. This makes the settings action appear available but do nothing when clicked.

`pick` is now `async` and is passed directly as a command `onSelect` handler, but the command runner does not await or catch promise rejections (it just calls `option.onSelect?.()`). If `openAttachmentPickerDialog` / IPC fails, this will surface as an unhandled promise rejection. Consider keeping `pick` synchronous and handling errors inside a fire-and-forget async IIFE (falling back to the hidden `<input type="file">` on failure).

Removed the unused listener map and `on()` test scaffold in 7901010415. The excess-property concern did not reproduce because the repository typechecks were already passing, but the dead setup was unnecessary.

No change needed here. This is one continuous optional chain: when `platform.updater` is absent, `platform.updater?.install().then(...).catch(...)` short-circuits to `undefined` rather than accessing `.then` on `undefined`. Both app and repository-wide strict typechecks pass.

Fixed in 7901010415. Missing updater capability now projects to the same inert action shape as the disabled updater state, so web settings render a disabled Check now button instead of a no-op action. Added regression coverage.

`sdkFor` expects the actual directory path (it passes `directory` through to `serverSDK.createClient`). Here it's being called with `key` (the normalized/trimmed `directoryKey(directory)`), which can change path semantics (notably on Windows/UNC paths) and is inconsistent with other call sites in this file (e.g. `bootstrapInstance` uses `sdkFor(directory)`). This can cause MCP connect/disconnect/authenticate to be issued for the wrong directory string.

The dynamic import path for the v2 dialog isn’t handled on failure. If the chunk fails to load (network error, bundler issue, etc.), the picker will never open and the caller won’t receive a cancellation result.

`load()` can apply results from an older navigation after `navigate()` has already switched roots. Because the async request isn’t tied to the current `navigation` token, stale responses can still mutate the tree and/or flip the global `error` flag (especially from background preloads).
The error UI string is hard-coded and bypasses the existing i18n system. This will show English-only text in non-English locales.

The startup refresh can restore stale OpenCode state after a server is removed. `initialize()` starts this unguarded refresh in the background, so a late result can repopulate `opencodeChecks[distro]` after `removeServer()` clears it. Please apply the same server-existence guard used by `refreshOpencodeCheckBackground()`.

`add(env)` is now parameterized with `env` (for the scoped `GIT_INDEX_FILE`), but the file-listing `git(...)` calls inside `Effect.all([...])` don’t receive `env`, so they still consult the shared snapshot index. That can reintroduce stale `index.lock` sensitivity and also defeats the intended optimization of seeding/staging against the temporary index. Consider passing `env` to both the `diff-files` and `ls-files` calls as well.

`sourceKey` currently concatenates the full patch/before/after contents into the cache key. For large diffs this duplicates huge strings on the main thread (defeating the goal of keeping diff work off the UI thread) and can significantly increase memory usage. Consider using a small checksum (ideally a sampled checksum for very large strings) in the key instead of embedding the full contents.

The `catch` path re-reads `event.data.id`. If the original failure was caused by an unexpected/invalid message payload (e.g. `event.data` is null or missing `id`), the error handler can throw again and the worker won’t send a failure response. Capture/validate the request `id` once and only post an error response when an `id` is available.

In environments where `Worker` is unavailable (SSR, older browsers, some test runners), `createPreparedDiff` currently returns an accessor that is always `undefined`, which makes all diff views render nothing. Consider falling back to synchronous preparation so diffs still render (even if slower) when workers aren’t supported.

The current `??` precedence means a model setting `options.streaming: true` will override a provider setting `options.streaming: false`, re-enabling streaming even though the provider explicitly opted out. If the intent is that *either* scope can disable streaming (and provider-level `false` can’t be bypassed), compute `disableStreaming` as an OR of both checks (e.g., model is false OR provider is false) rather than using nullish coalescing.

The assertion `not.toBe(true)` is fairly weak: it would still pass if `stream` is set to an unexpected non-boolean value. To more directly validate the behavior described in the test (“stream:false on the wire”), assert that `stream` is either explicitly `false` (or absent, if that’s considered equivalent) in a way that can’t be satisfied by unintended truthy values.

Intentional, and consistent with the rest of the codebase: model options already override provider options everywhere else (`{ ...provider.options, ...model.options }` in provider.ts). Making `streaming` invert that precedence would be surprising. Nothing auto-populates `options.streaming`, so a model-level `true` only happens when a user explicitly sets it — a deliberate per-model override of a provider default. Keeping model-wins precedence.

Good call — tightened to `expect(body.stream ?? false).toBe(false)` so it rejects absent *and* any unexpected truthy value, while still passing for the absent-stream case that doGenerate produces. Pushed in 0da9544.

This introduces a hard-coded permission key that is handled differently than the other permission flags (which are derived from `next.permission` or `cfg.experimental?.primary_tools`). To keep permission handling consistent and avoid future drift, derive `plan_exit` the same way (e.g., conditionally from `next.permission` rules or from the configured tool list), or centralize the list of default permission keys in one place so additions don’t require scattered hard-coded entries.

The new permission key uses snake_case (`plan_exit`) whereas nearby keys are single-token lowercase (`todowrite`, `task`). If the project convention is to avoid underscores in permission IDs, consider renaming this to match the established pattern (and ensure it aligns with whatever string is used in `next.permission` rules).

The nested ternary reduces readability and makes future additions (e.g., more encodings or options) harder to maintain. Prefer an explicit `switch (encoding)` or `if/else` chain so each encoding’s behavior is clearer and easier to extend.

The hashed-asset regex won’t match common multi-extension build artifacts like source maps (e.g. `index-<hash>.js.map`) because it only allows a single extension segment (`\\.\\w+$`). If you intend source maps (and other multi-extension files) to be immutable-cached as well, update the pattern to allow multiple extension segments (e.g. `(...)(\\.\\w+)+$`) or explicitly handle `.map`.

`FSUtil.mimeType(file)` is computed twice (once in `embeddedUIResponse` and again inside `cacheControl`). Consider changing `cacheControl` to accept the already-computed `mime` (or pass it in) to avoid duplicate work and keep the policy logic independent of re-deriving MIME type.

`self.clients.claim()` should be included in the `event.waitUntil(...)` chain; otherwise the activation can complete before claiming clients, leading to pages not being controlled until the next navigation/reload. Combine cache cleanup + `clients.claim()` into a single promise passed to `waitUntil`.

If `cached` is undefined and the network fetch fails, the `.catch(() => cached)` resolves to `undefined`, so `fresh` resolves to `undefined` and `respondWith` will receive a non-Response value (runtime error). The same pattern appears in the static-asset stale-while-revalidate path. Adjust the fallback logic so that when there is no cached response and the fetch fails, the promise rejects (or returns a valid fallback `Response`), rather than resolving to `undefined`.

A hard-coded cache name requires manual bumps to reliably invalidate cached non-hashed resources (notably `/index.html`). Consider deriving the cache version from a build identifier (or injecting it at build time) so deployments automatically roll caches without relying on developers to remember to rename it.

Swallowing registration failures makes service worker issues hard to diagnose. Consider at least logging the error in non-production builds (or reporting it) so failures (e.g., wrong scope/path, HTTPS requirements, script parse errors) are visible during development and can be acted on.

`deleteSession` now returns `true` immediately after scheduling the network delete, even if the server request fails later (the `.catch(...){ return false }` return value is not observed by the caller). This changes the function’s success semantics compared to the previous `await`-based implementation and can cause callers to treat a failed deletion as successful. Fix by either: (a) making `deleteSession` `async` again and awaiting the delete request (returning a boolean based on the result), or (b) changing the function contract to return `void` (or a `Promise<void>`) and updating call sites accordingly so they don’t rely on a synchronous boolean.

This changes the function’s success semantics compared to the previous `await`-based implementation and can cause callers to treat a failed deletion as successful. Fix by either: (a) making `deleteSession` `async` again and awaiting the delete request (returning a boolean based on the result), or (b) changing the function contract to return `void` (or a `Promise<void>`) and updating call sites accordingly so they don’t rely on a synchronous boolean.

`Binary.search` only produces correct results if `draft.session` is sorted by the key selector (`s.id`). The previous implementation used `findIndex`, which worked regardless of ordering. If `draft.session` is not strictly sorted by `id` at all times, this can remove the wrong element or fail to remove an existing session. Fix by switching back to `findIndex`/linear scan here, or (if the list is guaranteed sorted) enforce/document that invariant near the data structure and consider asserting it in development/tests.

The rollback path for deletion also relies on `Binary.search(draft.session, s.id, ...)`, which has the same sorted-by-id requirement as the optimistic removal path. If `draft.session` isn’t guaranteed sorted, rollback may insert sessions at incorrect positions or fail to detect existing entries properly. Fix by using an order-independent approach (e.g., `findIndex`) or by guaranteeing and documenting that `draft.session` remains sorted by `id`.

`.then((x) => x.data)` is currently a no-op because the resolved value isn’t used by subsequent code (and the chain isn’t returned/awaited). This makes the intent harder to read. Remove the `.then(...)` entirely, or (if you need the response) return/await the promise and use the result to drive the function’s return value or additional logic.

The `max-height` calculation hard-codes `140px`, which makes the layout brittle (it will drift if header/footer spacing changes). Consider replacing `140px` with a dedicated CSS custom property (e.g., `--question-prompt-chrome-height`) or deriving it from existing layout variables so the constraint stays consistent as the dock layout evolves.

Using `<Show when={!props.minimized}>` unmounts/remounts the content and footer when minimized, which can unintentionally reset internal component state, scroll position, and focus. If the intent is purely visual collapsing, prefer keeping the elements mounted and toggling visibility via CSS/attributes (e.g., `[hidden]`, `display: none`, `max-height: 0`, etc.) so state is preserved.

Injecting the entire plan file into the question can produce extremely large prompts (slow UI rendering, large network payloads, and/or excessive context for downstream agents). Consider truncating the included content (e.g., first N chars/lines with an explicit 'truncated' note), or summarizing + linking to the file path, while still preventing empty-plan exits.

Injecting the entire plan file into the question can produce extremely large prompts (slow UI rendering, large network payloads, and/or excessive context for downstream agents). Consider truncating the included content (e.g., first N chars/lines with an explicit 'truncated' note), or summarizing + linking to the file path, while still preventing empty-plan exits.

A `div` with `role=\"button\"` needs keyboard accessibility to behave like a real button (typically `tabIndex={0}`, `onKeyDown` handling for Enter/Space) and state signaling (e.g., `aria-expanded`). Alternatively, switch this element to a native `<button>` to get correct semantics and keyboard behavior by default.

Rendering question text as Markdown can introduce XSS risk if the Markdown renderer allows raw HTML or unsafe URL schemes. Ensure the `Markdown` component sanitizes output (or disables raw HTML) for untrusted text like `question()?.question`.

After removing the timeout-based delay, the readiness logic no longer needs timeout management. If `timer`/`window.clearTimeout` are still present elsewhere in this component (e.g., in `clear()`), consider removing the timeout-related state and branches to keep the cleanup logic minimal and avoid misleading future readers.

The memo name `messagesReady` no longer strictly reflects its logic (it can be true even when messages are not loaded as long as the session exists). To prevent confusion/misuse, rename this memo (e.g., to `sessionDataReady`) or split it into two memos (`messagesLoaded` and `sessionCached`) and combine them at the call site.

The render-time invocation `{sessionSync() ?? \"\"}` was removed. If `sessionSync()` previously established/maintained subscriptions, kicked off syncing, or ensured reactive tracking, removing it may prevent sync from starting (or change when it starts). If it’s still required, prefer calling it from a dedicated reactive effect (e.g., `createEffect`) rather than from JSX, so the side effect is explicit and not coupled to rendering.

Adding `overflow-hidden` on the session panel container will clip absolutely-positioned children. In this component the `ResizeHandle` (shown when `desktopReviewOpen()`) is `position: absolute` and uses a horizontal `translateX(50%)` (and optionally `-right-1`), so it can become partially/fully clipped and hard/impossible to grab when the review panel is open.

Fixed in cabb4d7973. The outer panel remains unclipped as the positioning context for ResizeHandle, while a new inner surface owns the background, radius, shadow, and clipping for both the timeline and composer.

Using the second argument to `.then()` only handles rejections from `find()`, but it will *not* catch errors thrown while mapping/normalizing the response. If `normalize()` (or unexpected response shape) throws, the returned promise will reject instead of falling back to `[]`. Using `.catch(() => [])` after the mapping covers both network failures and mapping/normalization errors.

The compat launcher is prod-only, but the regression also affected beta: the regressed `executableName: "opencode-desktop"` was shared across all channels, and the deb/rpm launcher filename falls back to `executableName`, so regressed beta packages also installed `/usr/share/applications/opencode-desktop.desktop`. Beta users who pinned during the regression window will lose their pins on upgrade.

This may well be an acceptable tradeoff (short window, small audience, and a beta compat file would need a different `Exec` — `/opt/OpenCode Beta/ai.opencode.desktop.beta` — while colliding with prod's compat file at the same path, a conflict the regressed packages already had). If it's intentional, worth a sentence in the PR description; otherwise beta needs its own legacy entry.

Optional hardening: the installed `.desktop` filename here comes from `executableName` only because `linux.syncDesktopName` defaults to `false` — the identity holds because `executableName === appId` and `desktopName === appId + ".desktop"` happen to agree. Setting `linux.syncDesktopName: true` derives the launcher filename from `desktopName` directly, which is the pattern the 26.15.x docs recommend, and app-builder-lib notes the default flips to `true` in v27 anyway. Same output today; just removes the implicit coupling. (Relatedly, the explicit `StartupWMClass` below is already the 26.15.x default when `desktopName` is set — harmless, fine to keep as documentation.)

Nit: the env restore runs after `await import(...)` without `try`/`finally`, so if the import throws, the mutated `OPENCODE_CHANNEL` leaks into subsequent tests. Only matters when the config module is already broken, but a `finally` would keep those failures isolated. Applies to both tests in this file.

Resolved: maintainer decision is that launcher pin continuity is out of scope — no migration needed for beta (or anywhere). Not blocking merge. Optional follow-up: since pin migration is the compat launcher's only purpose, the `opencode-desktop.desktop` resource, the two `fpm` mappings, and the compat test could be dropped entirely to simplify the config — fine either way.

Spreading `meta.icon` / `meta.commands` will throw a TypeError if either property is `undefined` or `null`. Since `projectMeta` may be partial, prefer spreading a default empty object (e.g., `...(meta.icon ?? {})` / `...(meta.commands ?? {})`) or conditionally merging only when the sub-object exists.

These two separate server sync calls update closely related icon state and can leave the server in a partial/inconsistent state if one call fails (or if the server applies updates in a last-write-wins way). Consider making this an atomic update (single API call that updates both override + color) or, if the API must remain split, ensure sequencing/error handling so failures are surfaced and state cannot drift silently.

`isPowerShell` mis-detects shells when `shell` includes extra arguments (e.g., `"pwsh.exe -NoProfile"`), because `path.basename(...)` will include the arguments and won’t match `POWERSHELL_SHELLS`. This will skip the PowerShell `-EncodedCommand` path unexpectedly. Consider extracting only the executable portion (first token), while still handling quoted paths, then run `basename` on that executable path.

The PowerShell helpers (`encodePowerShellCommand` / `withPowerShellUtf8Preamble`) are duplicated in both `packages/core/src/tool/bash.ts` and `packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts`. This increases the chance of drift (e.g., one preamble gets updated but the other doesn’t). Consider factoring these into a shared utility module (or exporting from one place) so both call sites share a single implementation.

Prepending statements before the user-provided PowerShell `command` can break valid scripts that require being the first statement in the script text (notably `param(...)` blocks and `#requires` directives). With the current prelude, those commands will error even though they would work when passed directly. Consider conditionally injecting the encoding prelude only when the command does not start with `param` / `#requires`, or inserting the prelude after an initial `#requires` region and/or `param` block when present.

The PowerShell detection + `encodedPowerShellCommand` logic is now duplicated between `packages/core/src/tool/bash.ts` and `packages/opencode/src/shell/shell.ts`. This increases the risk of divergence (e.g., if flags/preamble need changes later). Consider extracting a shared helper (in a common package/module accessible to both) or reusing the existing `Shell.args(...)`/PowerShell encoding helper from a single location to keep behavior consistent.

Good catch — this was a real issue. I updated the implementation so the UTF-8 setup is no longer prepended directly to the user-provided PowerShell script text.

The encoded command is now a small wrapper that sets the console encodings first, then decodes the original user command and invokes it as a separate scriptblock. That preserves script-level constructs like leading `param(...)` blocks and `#requires` directives, while still keeping the UTF-8 behavior.

Agreed. I extracted the PowerShell argument/encoding construction into a shared helper under `@opencode-ai/core`, and updated both execution paths to use it.

`packages/opencode/src/shell/shell.ts` now uses the shared PowerShell helper from `Shell.args(...)`, and `packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts` reuses `Shell.args(...)` instead of building its own PowerShell argv. The core BashTool also uses the same shared helper, so the `-EncodedCommand` wrapper behavior stays consistent across the direct shell, shell tool, and core BashTool paths.

Suggestion, feel free to ignore if you prefer a different approach. The account prompt validates trimmed input, but normalizeAccount keeps leading and trailing whitespace. An accidental space in the prompt will make the generated Snowflake host invalid, so consider trimming before stripping the URL/domain parts.

```suggestion
  return input.trim().replace(/^https?:\/\//, "").replace(/\.snowflakecomputing\.com\/?$/, "").replace(/\/+$/, "")
```

Suggestion, the human reviewer can decide how strict to be here. This handles an OAuth error callback before checking the returned state, so any request that reaches the loopback root with an `error` parameter can reject the pending authorization even when the state is missing or wrong. Since state is the CSRF guard for the callback, consider validating `pendingOAuth` and `state === pendingOAuth.state` before treating either success or error responses as terminal.

Suggestion, feel free to choose a different fix. This branch keys off the stored auth type, but `token` above can come from `SNOWFLAKE_CORTEX_TOKEN`, `SNOWFLAKE_CORTEX_PAT`, `input.options.token`, or `input.options.apiKey` before it falls back to `auth.access`. If a user has stored OAuth auth and then sets an env/config token to override it, the OAuth loader fetch from plugin options is preserved and will overwrite the request `Authorization` header with the stored OAuth access token. Consider basing this on the token source, or otherwise disabling the OAuth fetch wrapper when env/config token wins.

Rendering `` tags without a `src` can cause undesirable behavior in browsers (e.g., showing a broken-image icon, and in some cases triggering a request to the current document URL). Consider setting a safe placeholder `src` (e.g., a `data:,` URL) while keeping `data-local-image` for later resolution, or avoid emitting an `` until the path is resolved.

`data-local-image-resolved` is set before the resolver promise fulfills. If the resolver returns `undefined` or throws, the attribute remains and the image will never be retried (even though it was never actually resolved). A more robust approach is to mark a 'pending' state separately and only set 'resolved' after successfully assigning `img.src`, or remove the attribute in the `.catch` / `!dataUri` path so future renders can attempt again.

If the resolver returns `undefined` or throws, the attribute remains and the image will never be retried (even though it was never actually resolved). A more robust approach is to mark a 'pending' state separately and only set 'resolved' after successfully assigning `img.src`, or remove the attribute in the `.catch` / `!dataUri` path so future renders can attempt again.

The cache eviction behaves like FIFO rather than LRU because cache hits (`imageCache.get(cacheKey)`) do not update insertion order. This can evict frequently used entries. If the intent is LRU, refresh the key on hit (e.g., `delete` then `set`) or use a small dedicated LRU implementation so eviction matches expected behavior.

Using a broad `mimeType.startsWith(\"image/\")` allowlist may unintentionally permit `image/svg+xml`. Even when loaded via ``, SVG can carry additional risk (e.g., external references, historical browser quirks). Consider restricting to a safer set of raster types (e.g., `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`, `image/avif`) or explicitly excluding SVG if it’s not required.

The traversal check blocks literal `..` path segments, but it does not account for percent-encoded traversal sequences (e.g., `%2e%2e/`). If the server layer decodes/normalizes paths, this can bypass the client-side guard. Consider normalizing/decoding before validation (or only accepting a strict relative-path character set) in addition to server-side validation.

The same HTML-escaping logic is duplicated for `alt`, `title`, and local `href`. Consider extracting a small helper (e.g., `escapeAttr`) to reduce repetition and lower the chance of future inconsistencies.

`tabsAreOverflowing` is never initialized on mount anymore; it relies entirely on the first `ResizeObserver` callback firing. If the observer callback is delayed or doesn’t fire (e.g. element starts offscreen/`display:none`, or RO isn’t available), `forceTruncate` can stay wrong. Trigger an initial measurement right after wiring the observer.

Follow-up in `d45c0d8`: I changed this again after testing the chunk fallback. Stream chunk counts were too provider/model-dependent to present as token throughput, so the live footer now tracks committed response length, smooths it, and displays `Math.round(smoothedResponseLength / 4)` as an estimated token count. The `~` marker stays intentional, and provider-reported usage/cost still replaces the estimate when it arrives.

The resize handle wrapper is now outside the inner layer that gets `pointer-events-none` when the terminal is closed, so when `opened()` is false the handle can still intercept pointer events over the 8px strip above the collapsed panel (and potentially show a resize cursor / block clicks, depending on `inert` support). Disable pointer events for the handle while closed to preserve the prior behavior.

`getBoundingClientRect()` can return sub-pixel values depending on devicePixelRatio/rounding. Asserting exact `top`/`bottom` via `toEqual` may be flaky if the values come back as `-7.9999` etc. Consider rounding (or using a tolerant assertion) before comparing.

This `base64Encode` uses `btoa(value)` directly, which is not UTF-8 safe (and also depends on `btoa` being available in the test runner environment). Other e2e tests in this repo use a URL-safe base64 encoding based on `Buffer.from(value, "utf8")...`, which will correctly handle non-ASCII paths too.

`current()` returns `undefined` on both `home` and `dir-new-sesssion` routes. This makes tab-related commands (close/prev/next/mod+1..9) and the Home toggle logic treat those routes as having no current tab, so shortcuts won’t work from the session list route and the Home toggle can’t “return” to the last active tab from Home.

`canToggleHome()` disables the Home button/command on any non-home route where `current(route)` is `undefined` (e.g. the `/:dir/session` “dir-new-sesssion” route, or on initial load before the session tab is registered). That prevents navigating to Home via the Home button / mod+b even though going Home should always be possible; only the *return* action from Home needs an active tab.

This removes the macOS native-menu accelerator for `sidebar.toggle` (Cmd+B). Since Electron’s application menu uses `entry.accelerator?.macos` (see `packages/desktop/src/main/menu.ts`), this changes desktop behavior/visibility for the legacy layout as well, which conflicts with the PR goal of keeping the legacy sidebar shortcut behavior unchanged. If the intent is “Cmd+B toggles sidebar in legacy, but toggles Home in v2”, this likely needs a conditional accelerator selection based on the active layout design (requires changes in the desktop menu wiring).

Suggestion: this should probably also detect --port=1234 and --hostname=0.0.0.0 forms. With the current process.argv.includes("--port") checks, yargs still parses those explicit flags into args/network, but external stays false, so an explicitly requested external TUI can fall back to the internal worker transport and skip the served instance/auth path.

The badge currently receives `branchLabel()` (a truncated value), and then uses that value for both `title` and `aria-label`. This makes the full branch name inaccessible to tooltips and screen readers when it exceeds the truncation threshold. Prefer passing the full branch name into `ComposerBranchBadge` (and rely on CSS truncation for the visible text), or pass both `fullBranch` and `displayBranch` so `title`/`aria-label` can use the full value.
